state.tailText:
y: Medium
Exact failure mode: The contract states "Unchanged fingerprints, setup blockers, and cooldowns cause zero provider calls" but does not specify how cooldowns are persisted across process restarts or how fingerprint comparison interacts with CDP session state.
Minimal fix: Persist cooldowns and last-fingerprint in the append-only JSONL (or a small durable sidecar) with atomic updates. On CDP reconnect, re-validate fingerprint before any action.
Deterministic test: Restart the grounding service while a CDP session is active and a cooldown is in effect → assert no provider calls are made until cooldown expires and fingerprint is re-checked.
4. ReadDirectoryChangesW/Watchdog Overflow Recovery and the Hourly Reconciliation Contract
Finding 4.1
Severity: High
Exact failure mode: Native filesystem events debounce for 30 seconds with hourly full reconciliation for overflow/missed events. However, the exact semantics of ReadDirectoryChangesW (Windows) vs watchdog fallback, the precise debounce window behavior on rapid create/delete/rename bursts, and the exact reconciliation algorithm (what is compared, how conflicts with JSONL are resolved) are not specified.
Minimal fix: Document the debounce as a sliding window (last event + 30 s quiet period). Define reconciliation as a full directory walk + content fingerprint comparison against the last known JSONL state. On overflow, mark the reconciliation run with a special reconciliation_id event.
Deterministic test: Create 500 rapid file mutations (create/modify/delete/rename) in <30 s to trigger potential overflow → wait for debounce + next hourly reconciliation → assert all mutations appear exactly once in JSONL with correct lineage and no duplicates.
5. Integration Boundaries for NEXUSCLAW 8-Channel Memory and Durable ARCHIVIST Handoff
Finding 5.1
Severity: Critical
Exact failure mode: The contract mentions integration boundaries for NEXUSCLAW 8-channel memory and durable ARCHIVIST handoff but provides zero detail on the handoff protocol, channel mapping (which of the 8 channels receives GroundingEvents vs source cards), durability guarantees (exactly-once vs at-least-once), or back-pressure handling when ARCHIVIST is slow.
Minimal fix: Define a typed handoff envelope (GroundingEvent or SourceCard) with handoff_id, channel (0–7), priority, and retry_count. Use append-only JSONL as the durable queue; NEXUSCLAW consumes via tailing + ack. Implement bounded back-pressure (pause filesystem watcher when any channel queue exceeds threshold).
Deterministic test: Flood the system with 10 000 events while artificially slowing ARCHIVIST consumption on one channel → assert no data loss, correct channel routing, and eventual catch-up without unbounded memory growth.

Prioritized P0/P1/P2 Patch List
P0 (Critical – must fix before any production use)
Define and enforce GroundingEvent schema v1 + validation on append.
Implement crash-consistent append (atomic write + fsync) and corrupt-tail handling in rebuild.
Add explicit CDP connection manager with bounded retries and single-instance enforcement.
Define NEXUSCLAW handoff protocol with channel mapping and back-pressure.
P1 (High – required for correctness and auditability)
Add contradiction detection + routing in source-card promotion.
Formalize deletion/rename semantics and lineage DAG invariants.
Implement duplicate-tab detection and cooldown persistence across restarts.
Specify exact reconciliation algorithm and overflow marking.
P2 (Medium – operational robustness)
Add evidence-grade downgrade rules and secret/browser-store exclusion logging.
Expose reconciliation metrics and queue-depth observability to NEXUSCLAW.
Document CDP profile health-check and recovery playbook.
Claims That Could Not Be Verified from This Sandbox
Actual GroundingEvent schema definition or any example JSONL records.
Concrete implementation of ReadDirectoryChangesW vs watchdog fallback code.
Exact CDP connection manager or logon recovery logic.
NEXUSCLAW 8-channel memory layout or handoff consumer code.
Any runtime behavior under crash, overflow, or high-event-rate conditions.
Presence/absence of secret pattern detection or browser-store exclusion filters in the current build.
All claims above are derived solely from the verified local contract text and standard engineering analysis of the described mechanisms. No local files were read, modified, or executed.
